scope: Proposition 6.6 (Interior comparison across a fixed buffer) of the manuscript “SLE3 universality for weak finite-range Ising interactions” (preprints/SLE3-universality-for-weak-finite-range-Ising-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 44a7837e35328259), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 60. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a square Q and a larger square ̃ Q, with Q ⊂ int ̃ Q, in a fixed physical torus chart. Take lattice mesh δ ↓ 0, with torus side N chosen so that this chart has a fixed macroscopic buffer from its translates. Suppose every lattice vertex in ̃ Q is free in a domain spin law ντ Ω,λ. For all sufficiently small mesh there is a constant C < ∞, depending on the two fixed squares and the chart but not on Ω, τ, or the mesh, such that C−1 ≤ ντ Ω,λ(σQ∩δZ2 = η) µλ,N (σQ∩δZ2 = η) ≤ C for every spin configuration η. (6.11) The same bounds hold for every event determined by these spins. The exterior pins may be arbitrary, including those induced by any admissible exterior contour configuration.
